cultural_entities.gloss: Homeland, motherland, or country; a term deeply rooted in South Asian patriotic and emotional discourse.
cultural_entities.translation_note: The Urdu-derived term 'watan' carries a deep, emotionally charged sense of homeland, nation, or motherland in South Asian poetry, which is translated as 'country' in English.

annotation.emotional_arc: A steady, unifying declaration of shared ownership and belonging, moving from collective assertion to a tender, dream-filled embrace of the homeland.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation of 'watan' as 'country' loses the deep emotional, patriotic, and poetic resonance of the Urdu/Hindi word 'watan', which carries a strong sense of homeland, belonging, and shared identity.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The homeland is built upon, sustained by, and belongs to the collective love and aspirations of its people.
acceptable_visual_variants: A group of diverse citizens looking towards a bright horizon together
Hands holding soil together with small green shoots growing from it
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: The country belongs to/is made of your love and your dreams.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing literal floating hearts or sleeping people dreaming next to a physical map of a country, which misses the abstract sense of civic devotion and shared national hope.

metaphor_mapping.tenor_concept: abstract emotions and aspirations of citizens
metaphor_mapping.vehicle_concept: possessions or building blocks of a physical space

metaphor_spans.source_span_original:
तुम्हारी मुहब्बत का है,
तुम्हारे ही ख्वाबों का है।
metaphor_spans.source_span_translation:
It is the love of yours,
It is your dreams, too.
metaphor_spans.source_term:
तुम्हारी मुहब्बत का है,
तुम्हारे ही ख्वाबों का है।
metaphor_spans.tenor: The emotional and aspirational investment of the citizens in their nation
metaphor_spans.vehicle: Love and dreams as physical foundations or owners of a country
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a diverse group of people holding hands or working together to build a community, with subtle warm lighting symbolizing hope and shared dreams.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation of 'tumhari muhabbat ka hai' as 'It is the love of yours' and 'tumhare hi khwabon ka hai' as 'It is your dreams, too' flattens the possessive postposition 'ka' (of), which grammatically links the homeland directly as being 'made of' or 'born from' your love and dreams.

annotation.theme: The homeland belongs equally to everyone, built on shared love, dreams, and collective identity.

consistency_review_findings.issue: The translation_quality is marked as 'faithful', but there is a non-empty translation_loss array detailing a medium-severity loss of the emotional resonance of 'watan'. This is internally inconsistent.

original_poem:
यह वतन तुम्हारा है,
यह वतन हमारा है।
हम सबका है,
हम सबका है।
यह वतन तुम्हारा है,
यह वतन हमारा है।

तुम्हारी मुहब्बत का है,
तुम्हारे ही ख्वाबों का है।
हमारा वतन है,
हमारा वतन है।
यह वतन तुम्हारा है,
यह वतन हमारा है।
translated_poem:
This country belongs to you,
This country belongs to us.
It belongs to all of us,
It belongs to all of us.

It is the love of yours,
It is your dreams, too.
It is our country,
It is our country.
This country belongs to you,
This country belongs to us.
